g1.label: 1. Jonas’s concern
g1.why: Jonas says new colleagues may feel isolated when working remotely.

g2.correct: She extends the pilot to eight weeks
accept: She extends the pilot to eight weeks
g2.label: 2. Lena’s change
g2.why: Lena suggests running the pilot for eight weeks instead of six.

g3.label: 3. Jonas’s Friday task
g3.why: Maya asks Jonas to prepare the feedback questions by Friday.

g4.correct: To confirm the decisions and responsibilities
accept: To confirm the decisions and responsibilities
g4.label: 4. Purpose of Maya’s summary
g4.why: Her summary confirms the agreed pilot and each person’s responsibility.

g1.correct: I see your point, but have we considered the cost?
accept: I see your point, but have we considered the cost?
g1.label: 1. Acknowledge before disagreeing
g1.why: Acknowledging the other view before raising cost keeps the disagreement diplomatic.

g2.correct: I’m not sure that would work for our clients.
accept: I’m not sure that would work for our clients.
g2.label: 2. Soften a disagreement
g2.why: “I’m not sure” softens the disagreement while giving a client-related reason.

g3.correct: What if we tried a two-week pilot instead?
accept: What if we tried a two-week pilot instead?
g3.label: 3. Offer an alternative
g3.why: “What if” introduces a concrete alternative without imposing it.

g4.correct: Could you prepare the draft by Tuesday?
accept: Could you prepare the draft by Tuesday?
g4.label: 4. Assign an owner
g4.why: This polite request names the listener, task and deadline.

g5.correct: Nina will send the revised quote to the client by 3 p.m. on Friday.
accept: Nina will send the revised quote to the client by 3 p.m. on Friday.
g5.label: 5. Specific action point
g5.why: The action point includes an owner, task, recipient and exact deadline.

g6.correct: Let’s move on to the next item on the agenda.
accept: Let’s move on to the next item on the agenda.
g6.label: 6. Spaced recall from Business Meetings
g6.why: Business Meetings used this phrase to move to the next agenda item.
